AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To consider the potential of self-help relaxation training to treat depression after stroke.

AbstractText.Label: DESIGN
AbstractText.content: Randomized controlled trial with cross-over at three months.

AbstractText.Label: PARTICIPANTS
AbstractText.content: In total, 21 people with stroke, aged 49-82 years.

AbstractText.Label: MAIN MEASURE
AbstractText.content: Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale-Depression (HADS-D) subscale.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: No difference in depression change scores was identified between the treatment and control groups; however, on two follow-ups, significant positive differences relative to screening were found for the treatment group (at 2 months Z = -2.55, P = .011 and 12 months Z = -2.44, P = .015). A partial η2 = .07 was identified.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Self-help relaxation holds promise as a self-help treatment for depression after stroke. Findings from this trial, considered with others of relaxation for depression, suggest that a study including a total of 80 participants would likely be sufficient to establish efficacy of the treatment, relative to controls, in those with stroke.
